title: Error Budget Policy Templates and Automation Scripts
author: Priya Sharma
content:
Overview
--------
This document provides a set of standardized error budget policy templates and accompanying automation scripts for Redwood Inference services. It is intended to reduce decision latency during SLO burn events, ensure consistent operational response, and enable safe, auditable automation for capacity and throttling actions.

Scope and intended audience
-------------------------
- Audience: SREs, Service Owners, Platform Engineers, Oncall Responders.
- Scope: Multi-tenant inference services (hosted API, Dedicated pools) and platform-level routing/orchestration components.
- Non-goal: This document does not replace contractual SLA processes; it is focused on operational SLO governance and internal mitigations.

Why templates and automation?
---------------------------
- Reduce ambiguity: consistent tiers and actions minimize cross-team coordination during incidents.
- Faster mitigation: automated, reversible actions reduce mean time to remediation (MTTR).
- Auditability: standardized templates produce predictable audit trails and allow post-incident analysis.

Key concepts and glossary
------------------------
- SLO: Service Level Objective (e.g., p99 latency < 300ms over 7d).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (allowable fraction of bad events in the SLO window).
- Burn rate: rate of error budget consumption relative to a baseline.
- Tier: classification of service criticality (Critical / High / Standard / Dev).
- Escalation action: predefined mitigation (scale up, token-gate, throttle non-critical tenants, degrade fidelity).

Policy templates (summary)
-------------------------
We provide three policy templates that map burn behavior to actions. Each template includes thresholds, automated actions, human approvals, and rollback conditions. Copy-and-edit these templates for service-specific adoption.

1) Conservative automation (recommended for Critical services)
- Burn thresholds: 2x sustained for 10m -> page oncall; 4x sustained for 5m -> auto-scale attempt + page; 10x sustained for 3m -> activate emergency routing to fallback model and reduce burst capacity for non-pay tiers.
- Human gate: require paging and >=1 engineer acknowledgement before tenant eviction.
- Rollback: stable burn rate <= 0.5x for 15m and latency p95 within target for 30m.

2) Operational automation (recommended for High/Standard services)
- Burn thresholds: 3x sustained for 10m -> auto-scale; 6x sustained for 5m -> apply token-priority throttle for non-critical tokens; 12x for 2m -> route traffic to cheaper or quantized model variant.
- Human gate: auto-scale does not require approval; tenant throttle requires approval if >5% traffic impact.
- Rollback: same as above but with 10m stabilization windows.

3) Fast-fail automation (Dev / Testing environments)
- Burn thresholds: 1.5x for 5m -> immediate soft-eviction of noisy tenants; 3x for 1m -> hard eviction.
- Human gate: none. Intended for safety in sandboxed environments.

Configuration table (copy into service policy)
----------------------------------------------
| param | description | example |
| SLO_name | short id for SLO | inference-latency-p99-7d |
| owner | primary owner (team/person) | team:runtime, owner:alice@redwood.com |
| SLI | measured signal | p99_latency_ms, success_rate |
| target | numeric target | p99 < 300ms, success_rate >= 99.5% |
| window | evaluation window | 7d |
| error_budget | 1 - target | 0.005 |
| tiers | critical/high/standard/dev | high |
| burn_thresholds | list of numeric multipliers + durations | ["2x:10m","4x:5m","10x:3m"] |
| auto_actions | ordered list of action ids | ["autoscale_1","throttle_nonpay","fallback_route_2"] |
| human_gate | yes/no and approvers | yes: oncall@pagerduty |
| rollback_criteria | stabilization rules | p95 within target for 30m & burn <= 0.5x for 15m |

Automation patterns and recommended architecture
------------------------------------------------
1) Alerting -> Policy Engine -> Orchestrator -> Action Executors
- Alerting: Prometheus/Tempo/Traces and SLI exporters produce alerts when burn thresholds are crossed.
- Policy Engine: a lightweight service that evaluates the policy templates and decides actions; stores decisions in an immutable event log.
- Orchestrator: executes approved automation (Kubernetes API, autoscaler, routing control-plane) and records the outcome.
- Action Executors: scripts/playbooks (bash/Python), infra APIs, or cloud scaling calls.

Design principles
- Idempotency: actions must be safe to retry.
- Reversibility: every action must have a clearly defined rollback path.
- Observable: actions emit events with correlation ids to SLI telemetry.
- Least privilege: action runners use scoped credentials and must be auditable.

Sample Prometheus alert rule (burn rate)
--------------------------------------
```yaml
groups:
- name: slo-error-budget
  rules:
  - alert: ErrorBudgetBurnHigh
    expr: (sum(rate(slo_burn_estimate_total[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(slo_burn_window_total[5m])) by (service)) > 3
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "{{ $labels.service }} high error budget burn"
      description: "Burn rate > 3x for 10m."
```

PagerDuty & notification guidance
---------------------------------
- Severity mapping: page -> P1 oncall; ticket -> P2 queue; info -> slack channel #sre-observability.
- PagerDuty runbooks should include exact runbook link and event id.

Example GitHub Actions workflow (create a mitigation issue)
----------------------------------------------------------
```yaml
name: Create-error-budget-issue
on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [error_budget_burn]
jobs:
  create_issue:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Create GitHub issue for mitigation
        uses: peter-evans/create-issue@v4
        with:
          title: "[AUTOMATION] Error budget burn: ${{ github.event.client_payload.service }}"
          body: |
            Service: ${{ github.event.client_payload.service }}\n            Burn multiplier: ${{ github.event.client_payload.multiplier }}\n            Suggested action: ${{ github.event.client_payload.suggested_action }}\n```

Sample autoscale executor (bash)
--------------------------------
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scale-service.sh SERVICE_NAME desired_replicas
SERVICE=$1
REPLICAS=$2
set -euo pipefail
kubectl -n inference scale deploy ${SERVICE} --replicas=${REPLICAS}
# emit an event to policy engine
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"'${SERVICE}'","action":"scale","replicas":'${REPLICAS}'}' \
  https://policy-engine.internal/api/v1/actions
```

Safe rollback recipe
--------------------
1) Pause further automation: set policy engine to manual mode.
2) Revert routing rules to prior version using config id and wait 5 minutes.
3) Gradually return capacity using the inverse autoscale policy in 10% increments every 3m while monitoring SLOs.
4) Create post-incident action item to adjust thresholds if needed.

SLO simulation playground (how-to)
---------------------------------
Purpose: test policy templates and automation safely before production rollout.
Steps: 
1) Create an isolated sandbox cluster/namespace labeled owner=sim-playground.
2) Deploy a canary service configured with the target SLO and a traffic generator (vegeta or k6).
3) Drive load profiles that emulate realistic tenant noise patterns: short bursts, steady elevated load, choppy error spikes.
4) Observe policy engine decisions and executors in the sandbox. Validate idempotency and rollback procedures.
Commands (example):
```bash
# start load test
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m loadtest.js --env SERVICE=inference-canary
# monitor burn rate
kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus 9090:9090
# trigger a manual repo dispatch for GitHub Actions scenario
curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}' \
  https://api.github.com/repos/redwood-inference/infra/dispatches \
  -d '{"event_type":"error_budget_burn","client_payload":{"service":"inference-canary","multiplier":6,"suggested_action":"autoscale"}}'
```

Testing checklist before production enablement
--------------------------------------------
- [ ] Run 3 simulation profiles (burst, steady, erratic) for each policy template.
- [ ] Verify action idempotency by re-triggering same alert twice.
- [ ] Validate rollback criteria and automated revert.
- [ ] Confirm auditing events appear in central event log with correlation id.
- [ ] Security review of runner credentials and least-privilege role bindings.

Ownership, cadence, and metrics to track
---------------------------------------
- Policy owner: runtime-sre@redwood.com
- Automation owner: infra-automation@redwood.com
- Review cadence: quarterly policy review aligned with SLO quarterly review.
- Success metrics: mean MTTR reduction for error budget events, fraction of mitigations executed automatically, false-positive rate of automation triggers.

Playbook for oncall when automation runs
----------------------------------------
1) When alerted, check the policy-engine event ID and the action executed.
2) Confirm the event against the sandbox replay or telemetry.
3) If automation has degraded critical traffic, immediately run rollback recipe and escalate to the owner.
4) Post-incident, run the SLO simulation for the observed noise pattern and iterate thresholds.

Change and rollout process
-------------------------
1) Author a policy as a PR in the infra repo including the YAML policy + evidence from simulations.
2) Run automated unit tests in the CI (policy engine unit tests) and run the simulation suite.
3) Staged rollout: enable in sandbox -> enable in non-critical cluster -> enable for a small percentage of production traffic (canary) -> full rollout.
4) Document changes in the policy changelog and link to the related incident if applicable.

Appendix: quick reference commands
---------------------------------
- Pause automation: curl -X POST https://policy-engine.internal/api/v1/control -d '{"mode":"manual"}'
- Force rollback: curl -X POST https://policy-engine.internal/api/v1/actions/rollback -d '{"event_id":"<id>"}'
- Replay an event in sandbox: curl -X POST https://policy-engine.internal/api/v1/events -d '{"service":"inference-canary","metric":"burn","multiplier":5}'
